findings.location: Methods p.7 ('20% (62 samples) ... reserved for model testing') vs data/training_data.csv
findings.evidence: The paper says the test set is 20% of the combined data taken from study 16 (Shi et al.), i.e. 62 of 116 samples, and that the other 54 are used for training. The released training_data.csv contains rows with the test-set conditions (T=21.671875, ICorg=12.51, A=168, Bt=450, P=1.058, Cfit=2.6, to=37, Pv=0.1), which are outside the test ranges given in Table S2 (T 10-20, ICorg 7.725-21.7, A 70-340, Bt 180).

findings.location: Methods p.9 ('5-fold cross-validation') vs code R2_FeedBi_N.py:176-300
findings.evidence: The 5-fold CV is used only to compute train/validation R2 inside the training data; the test-set R2 is computed from the model fitted on the last fold only (model.predict(X_test) after the fold loop, R2_FeedBi_N.py:296-300), so the reported test R2 comes from a model trained on 4/5 of the training data, not on all of it.

The target and the features are standardised with scalerT/scalery fitted separately on the training and on the test set (scalerT.fit_transform(X_testl), scalery.fit_transform(y_test)), i.e. test-set statistics enter the preprocessing; the paper does not describe this.

findings.location: Methods p.8-9; Table 1 rows PCA/KPCA/Autoencoder; Figs. S4-S6
findings.evidence: The released capsule (code/BP.py, BP_LR.py, R2_FeedBi_N.py, sMAPE_FeedBi_N.py, Algo_comp_plot.py) contains no PCA, KernelPCA, Autoencoder, RandomForest, GradientBoosting, SVR or SHAP call (grep over 5 .py files: only the string 'PCA-NN' inside the hard-coded dict of Algo_comp_plot.py:7). Table 1/2 report 15 PCA/KPCA/Autoencoder/ensemble rows and Figs. S4-S6 report SHAP values, but no code that produces them is in the capsule.
